questions.title: What is the intuition behind GPU memory hierarchy impacting FlashAttention performance?
questions.question_body: In the background section the paper describes the GPU memory hierarchy (GMEM, L2, SMEM, RMEM) and mentions that FlashAttention‑2 achieves only 35% utilization on H100. I’m unclear how the different bandwidths and capacities of these memories translate into the observed bottleneck. Could someone explain, perhaps with a simple example, why an algorithm that eliminates intermediate global‑memory reads/writes still suffers low utilization, and how the new Warp‑Specialization scheme addresses this issue?

questions.title: How does the two‑stage WGMMA‑softmax pipelining actually overlap operations?
questions.question_body: Algorithm 3 in the paper shows a 2‑stage pipeline where the second WGMMA of iteration $j$ is overlapped with softmax of iteration $j+1$. I’m struggling to see how the dependencies are broken. What does "next" and "current" specifically refer to in terms of memory buffers, and how does the compiler preserve the ordering of the GEMMs and softmax operations? Would a toy schedule (e.g., a timeline with time steps) help clarify the overlap?

questions.title: Why is the FP8 WGMMA limited to k‑major operands and what does that imply for matrix layouts?
questions.question_body: Section 3.2 says that FP8 WGMMA only accepts k‑major operands, unlike FP16 where both mn‑major and k‑major are allowed. I understand that this is a hardware restriction, but I’m confused about how it influences the layout of the input matrices when computing attention. Specifically, how does this affect the packing of the value matrix V, and why does it necessitate either a pre‑processing transpose or an in‑kernel transpose? Could you walk through a concrete example of the memory layout before and after the transposition?

questions.title: What is block quantization and how does it reduce FP8 numerical error?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions block quantization as keeping one scalar per block (e.g., per B_r × d block). I’d like to understand how this works in practice. Does each block get its own scale factor that is applied during the dot‑product, and how is this incorporated into the softmax computation? Also, how does this interact with the scaling used for Q, K, V during quantization—do we apply the block scale to the quantized values or to the outputs?

questions.title: How does incoherent processing help with outlier values in FP8 attention?
questions.question_body: The authors propose multiplying Q and K by a random orthogonal matrix M before quantizing to FP8, claiming that this spreads out outliers. Could someone explain mathematically why this does not alter the attention output? Also, what is the cost of generating and applying M, and how is it fused with rotary embeddings as claimed?

questions.title: Why does FP8 FlashAttention‑3 achieve higher utilization than FP16 on Hopper?
questions.question_body: The results show that FP8 reaches close to 1.2 PFLOPs/s while FP16 achieves up to 740 TFLOPs/s. Since FP8 is half the precision of FP16, I would expect lower throughput unless the algorithm is specifically optimized. What aspects of the FP8 kernel (e.g., operand packing, register reuse, pipeline depth) allow it to outperform the FP16 kernel in terms of TFLOPs/s? Is the 2× throughput gain simply due to the hardware, or are there additional algorithmic modifications?

questions.title: How does the ping‑pong scheduling with warp‑specialization reduce exponential latency?
questions.question_body: The paper explains that exponential operations are 256× slower than FP16 matmul, so they use a ping‑pong schedule to overlap exp with GEMM. I’d like a clearer picture: how many warps are dedicated to each role, how the barriers (`bar.sync`) are set up, and how this schedule avoids idle cycles. Is there a simple diagram or pseudo‑timeline that shows the sequence of operations across two warp‑groups?

questions.title: What are the practical trade‑offs in choosing the number of stages `s` for the circular SMEM buffer?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 1 the authors mention an `s`‑stage circular SMEM buffer but do not give guidelines for selecting `s`. How does `s` affect register pressure, debugging complexity, and the ability to hide latency? In particular, what happens if `s` is too small or too large relative to the key block size `B_c` and query block size `B_r`?

questions.title: Why is the accumulator layout different from the operand layout in FP8 WGMMA, and how do you reconcile them?
questions.question_body: Section 3.2.2 describes a mismatch between the layout of the FP32 accumulator and the FP8 operand when performing two successive WGMMA operations. Could we walk through a small example (e.g., a 4×4 matrix) showing the register arrangement for the accumulator of the first GEMM and the operand of the second GEMM, and then illustrate the byte‑permutations needed to convert one into the other?

questions.title: How does the empirical evaluation account for different memory bandwidths across head dimensions?
questions.question_body: In the benchmarking section, the authors compare across head dimensions 64, 128, 256. I notice that larger head dimensions lead to higher arithmetic intensity but also potentially higher register allocation per thread. Could someone explain how FlashAttention‑3 balances register pressure with memory bandwidth to achieve its reported TFLOPs/s, especially when scaling up the head dimension?

questions.title: What is the effect of causal masking on the FP8 kernel performance?
questions.question_body: The results mention that for head dimensions 128 and 256, FP8 is at par or behind with causal masking. Why does causal masking reduce the performance benefits of FP8? Does it change the memory access pattern or the depth of the pipeline, and how might the algorithm be modified to better handle causal masks in low‑precision?
